item.subject: science
item.stem: Meera's class is discussing why Earth can support life. Her teacher says that rocks, soil, minerals, and the variety of landforms are not just a lifeless background. Which statement best explains how these support living things?

options.A: Rocks are non-living, so they cannot help living things survive.
options.B: Rocks only make the Earth look different from other planets.
options.C: Soil formed from broken-down rocks and the remains of plants and animals holds nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, and varied landforms create different habitats where living things can grow and survive.
options.D: Minerals in the Earth's crust are useful mainly for making buildings and roads.
